items.title: exfatprogs: 1.4.4 -> 1.4.5

items.content_html:
Hi! Setting the label of an exFAT filesystem through udisks fails on NixOS, for example from a udisks client such as GNOME Disks:

Cannot change exfat filesystem label on /dev/sda1: executable tune.exfat not found

udisks 2.11 handles exFAT through libblockdev 3, whose exFAT plugin runs mkfs.exfat, fsck.exfat and tune.exfat (exfat.c). The udisks package puts the FUSE-based exfat package on udisksd's PATH, and that package has no tune.exfat. This PR switches udisks to exfatprogs, which provides all three. I checked the options libblockdev passes (mkfs.exfat -n, tune.exfat -L, -I and -v, fsck.exfat -n) against exfatprogs 1.4.4.

Mounting doesn't change: libmount looks for mount helpers such as mount.exfat in its configured helper directories, not in udisksd's PATH, so the FUSE mount.exfat on that PATH was never used.

One side effect: Filesystem.Check on a damaged exFAT filesystem now fails with an error instead of returning false. exfatprogs' fsck.exfat -n exits with 4 when it finds errors, the FUSE one exited with 1, and libblockdev only treats exit code 1 as "not clean" (exfat.c). The damage is still reported, only as an error. Every distribution that ships exfatprogs has the same behavior, and I've sent a fix to libblockdev in storaged-project/libblockdev#1226.

The second commit extends nixosTests.udisks2 to format a loop device as exFAT and relabel it. The test fails on master with the error above and passes with the first commit.

The same bug exists on release-26.05, so this may be worth backporting.

I used Claude Code (Claude Opus 5.5) to investigate, write and test this change and this description, and reviewed both myself.

I reviewed this first in my fork, in davidvornholt#1. Since then I've rebased it onto current master, where the test derivation is unchanged, and corrected the commit message's sentence about mounting.

Add a NixOS module for Paseo, a daemon that orchestrates coding agents (Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode, ...) from desktop and mobile clients. Adapted from upstream's nix/module.nix, trimmed to nixpkgs conventions.

  • Add services.paseo with user, group, dataDir, listenAddress, port, openFirewall, extraPackages, settings and environmentFile
  • Render settings (RFC 42, JSON) to $PASEO_HOME/config.json on every start; relay and hostnames are configured there instead of dedicated options
  • Pass secrets such as PASEO_PASSWORD through environmentFile
  • Always put bash, git and procps on the service PATH; without ps the terminal worker fails to start
  • Add nixosTests.paseo, checking /api/health, terminal worker startup and the generated config.json
  • Wire the test into paseo.passthru.tests
  • Add a 26.11 release note entry

items.content_html:
PHP had two releases with a bunch of security vulns and that's also pretty exposed software.

For now it's still root that the service runs at[1], so this greatly reduces the surface already. I'm trying to get things done here that apply to 99% of all software and thus qualify as default without chasing regressions.

Two noteworthy things:

  • MemoryDenyWriteExecute=no doesn't seem doable due to PCRE2 use (pcre.jit=on) and I could trivially trigger test failures in multiple applications because of this. Needs more work if feasible at all.

  • SystemCallFilter=@System-service seems a sensible default. ~@privileged broke at least the Nextcloud's mail test:

      nextcloud # [74375.719442] nextcloud phpfpm-nextcloud-pre-start[398]: chown: changing ownership of '/run/phpfpm-nextcloud/credentials/mail_smtppassword': Operation not permitted
  nextcloud # [74375.719686] nextcloud phpfpm-nextcloud-pre-start[398]: chown: changing ownership of '/run/phpfpm-nextcloud/credentials/': Operation not permitted
  nextcloud # [74378.658793] nextcloud systemd[1]: phpfpm-nextcloud.service: Control process exited, code=exited, status=1/FAILURE

[1] Follow-up would be to also look into changing this.

items.content_html:
Follow-up to commit f20cd90 (where log() was defined for missing argument errors).

Options like --file and --attr properly check if an argument was provided:

--file|-f)
    if [ -z "$1" ]; then
        log "$0: '$i' requires an argument"
        exit 1
    fi

However, other flags consuming arguments (--root, --channel, --system, --flake, --max-jobs) unconditionally ran shift 1. When invoked with a trailing flag without an argument (e.g. nixos-install --root), shift 1 fails on an empty parameter list, causing bash to silently abort with exit code 1 under set -e.

Changes:

  • Add [ -z "$1" ] checks before shifting for --max-jobs, --root, --system, --flake, and --channel.
  • Report $0: '$i' requires an argument via log and exit with 1.

Testing:

$ nix-build -A nixos-install
/nix/store/znqsv634klrargdgha5nz6j390cxmjv2-nixos-install

$ ./result/bin/nixos-install --root
./result/bin/nixos-install: '--root' requires an argument
$ echo $?
1

$ ./result/bin/nixos-install --channel
./result/bin/nixos-install: '--channel' requires an argument
$ echo $?
1

$ ./result/bin/nixos-install --max-jobs
./result/bin/nixos-install: '--max-jobs' requires an argument
$ echo $?
1

Adds boot.loader.limine.expandGenerations which controls whether the top-level generation directories/groups in the boot menu are expanded by default. Defaults to true, matching current behaviour.

As per Limine's config docs, a directory entry is expanded by default if its name is prefixed with +. When the option is false, the + is omitted.

I've tested this on my machine by replacing the stock module with this diff. Disabling the option rightly makes the entry collapsed.

items.content_html:
Overview

This PR adds a NixOS module for opencode, an AI coding agent.

NixOS module (nixos/modules/services/misc/opencode.nix):

  • Multiple named server instances via services.opencode.servers.<name>
  • Secure authentication: password via systemd LoadCredential (passwordFile) or plaintext (password); no unauthenticated mode
  • Per-instance JSONC settings written to /etc/opencode-<name>/opencode/opencode.jsonc
  • Isolated state directory at /var/lib/opencode-<name> for database, logs, sessions
  • Optional firewall integration per instance
  • Version enforcement: requires opencode 2.x (refuses older at evaluation)

NixOS test (nixos/tests/opencode.nix):

  • Two VMs covering both password modes, settings, state directory, basic auth, and custom user/group

items.content_html:
When nixos-enter is invoked with an option requiring an argument (--root, --system, or --command/-c) as the final parameter, the script unconditionally executes shift 1 on an empty parameter list:

$ sudo nixos-enter --root
$ echo $?
1

Because shift 1 fails on the empty positional parameters and set -e is active, the script silently aborts with exit code 1 without providing any diagnostic message to the user.

Changes:

  • Add a check [ -z "$1" ] before shifting for --root, --system, and --command/-c
  • Output $0: '$i' requires an argument to stderr and exit with 1

Testing:

Verified manually with ./result/bin/nixos-enter:

$ ./result/bin/nixos-enter --root
./result/bin/nixos-enter: '--root' requires an argument
$ echo $?
1

$ ./result/bin/nixos-enter -c
./result/bin/nixos-enter: '-c' requires an argument
$ echo $?
